channel.title: EngineerzCorneR — Posts
channel.description: Deep-dive technical write-ups across Electrical, Mechanical, HVAC, Automation, Civil and Solar.

item.title: HVAC & Plumbing Default Design Values: The Quick Reference
item.description: Common default design values for HVAC and plumbing — duct and pipe velocities, pressure drops, ACH, noise criteria, fresh air rates, temperatures, and plumbing velocities, pressures and slopes — for a first-pass sizing check.

item.title: 33/11 kV Substation: Single Line Diagram & Equipment Overview
item.description: How a 33/11 kV substation is built, walked through its single line diagram from incoming line to distribution feeders — every major equipment item, its function, and the protection schemes that back it up.

item.title: Access Control System (ACS) Explained: Components, Architecture & Site Work
item.description: How an Access Control System actually works — main components, the six-step credential-to-unlock sequence, system architecture, integration with FAS/BMS/CCTV, and what an electrical site engineer does on an ACS install.

item.title: Electrical Panel Factory Acceptance Test (FAT): The Complete Checklist
item.description: The 8 stages of an LV panel FAT — visual and mechanical inspection, insulation resistance, hi-pot, functional, protection and interlock tests, and documentation — plus the acceptance criteria that close it out.

item.title: Flame Retardant vs Flame Resistant Cables: Know the Difference
item.description: IEC 60332 vs IEC 60331 explained — why flame retardant cables stop fire from spreading while flame (fire) resistant cables keep circuits alive during a fire, plus where each belongs.

item.title: Air Changes per Hour: What ACH Actually Tells You (and Doesn't)
item.description: What air changes per hour (ACH) measures, the airflow ÷ volume formula behind it, typical ACH targets by space type, and why short-circuiting or dead zones can hit the number on paper without actually ventilating the room.

item.title: Reading a Psychrometric Chart: The Five Lines That Matter
item.description: How dry-bulb temperature, humidity ratio, relative humidity, wet-bulb temperature and enthalpy combine on a psychrometric chart, and how to trace a cooling or dehumidification process across it.

item.title: K-Rated Transformers: What K-Factor Means and When You Need One
item.description: What a K-rated transformer actually is, the IEEE C57.110 K-factor scale from K-1 to K-20, how it differs in construction from a standard transformer, and the applications where K-13 is the common default.

item.title: BMS Point Types Explained: AI, AO, BI, BO, MI, MO, BV, AV, MV
item.description: What each BMS point abbreviation actually means — AI, AO, BI, BO, MI, MO, BV, AV and MV — the signal ranges behind them, and why the virtual points (BV/AV/MV) don't correspond to any physical wiring at all.

item.title: Harmonics in Power Systems: Sources, Effects and How to Mitigate Them
item.description: Where harmonics come from, how IEEE 519 limits voltage THD at the point of common coupling, what unmanaged harmonics do to cables, transformers and capacitors, and the passive filter, active filter, K-rated transformer and reactor options to control them.

item.title: IEC 61439 Forms of Construction: Form 1 to Form 4 Explained
item.description: What Form 1 through Form 4 switchboard construction actually separates inside an LV panel, the 2a/2b, 3a/3b and 4a/4b sub-variants, and why the Form number is a deliberate specification choice, not a manufacturing default.

item.title: Retaining Wall Design Basics: Why Overturning, Sliding & Bearing All Have to Pass
item.description: The three independent stability checks behind every gravity or cantilever retaining wall — overturning, sliding, and bearing pressure — with the safety-factor thresholds engineers actually design to.

item.title: Beam Bending Basics: Why Section Modulus Decides Capacity, Not Just Load
item.description: Why a beam's bending capacity comes down to two separate checks — bending stress against section modulus, and deflection against span — not just the applied load.

item.title: Rebar Development Length: Why Bar Diameter Decides the Embedment, Not Rules of Thumb
item.description: Why development length is a function of bar diameter and concrete/steel strength rather than a flat number, how lap splices scale off it, and what hooks buy you.

item.title: Column Axial Capacity: Why Reinforcement Ratio and Slenderness Both Matter
item.description: How gross area and steel ratio combine into a short column's axial capacity, why codes cap reinforcement ratio at both ends, and when slenderness cuts that capacity down.

item.title: Staircase Geometry: The Riser-Tread Rule That Keeps Stairs Walkable
item.description: Why comfortable stairs come down to one relationship between riser height and tread depth, the typical ranges each falls within, and where headroom and going length come in.

item.title: Grade & Slope: Why Percent, Ratio and Degrees Aren't the Same Number
item.description: How rise over run converts between percent grade, a ratio like 1:20, and an angle in degrees — and why mixing up the three is a common site-drawing mistake.

item.title: Trench Safe Slope: Why OSHA Soil Type Decides the Angle, Not the Depth
item.description: Why the same trench depth needs a completely different sloping angle depending on soil classification, what separates Type A, B and C soil, and when sloping stops being enough.

item.title: Cut & Fill Volume: How the Average End Area Method Actually Works
item.description: How earthwork volume between two cross-sections is estimated by averaging their areas, why section spacing controls accuracy, and where the method breaks down.

item.title: Slab-on-Grade Thickness: What Actually Drives the Number
item.description: Why slab-on-grade thickness comes from load, subgrade support and concrete strength together — not a flat default — and why the subgrade matters as much as the slab itself.

item.title: Manning's Equation: How Pipe Slope, Roughness and Diameter Set Flow Capacity
item.description: How Manning's equation turns pipe slope, roughness and diameter into gravity flow capacity, why full-bore isn't peak capacity, and what the roughness coefficient actually represents.

item.title: Concrete Volume Takeoff: From Cubic Meters to Bags of Cement
item.description: How a concrete volume gets converted into cement, sand and aggregate quantities using mix ratios, why wastage factors are added, and what water-cement ratio does to the mix.

item.title: Solar Panel Tilt & Orientation: Why Latitude Isn't the Whole Answer
item.description: How tilt angle and azimuth are chosen for fixed solar arrays, why the 'tilt equals latitude' rule of thumb only gets you to a starting point, and how seasonal weighting changes the answer.

item.title: MPPT vs PWM Solar Charge Controllers: What Actually Changes
item.description: Why an MPPT controller can pull 20-30% more power than PWM from the same panel, when PWM is still the right call, and how to actually size either one against your battery voltage.

item.title: Solar Panel Derating: Why Nameplate Wattage Isn't What You Get
item.description: The STC nameplate rating on a solar panel assumes lab conditions no rooftop ever sees. A walk through every real-world derate factor and typical loss ranges for each.

item.title: Signal Scaling: Turning a 4–20mA Loop Into an Engineering Value
item.description: How a PLC or DCS converts a raw 4-20mA transmitter signal into an engineering unit like level, pressure, or flow — the linear scaling formula, span vs. zero, and why untidy ranges cause quiet errors.

item.title: What Is an ELV System? Types, Components & the BIM Engineer's Role
item.description: Extra Low Voltage systems explained: the six categories (ICT, security, fire alarm, PA/voice evacuation, BMS, and more), how ELV differs from electrical power systems, and where MEP BIM fits in.

item.title: PLC vs DDC: What Actually Separates Them
item.description: PLC and DDC controllers both automate equipment, but they're built for different jobs. Purpose, communication protocols, programming, I/O handling, and when to use each.

item.title: IS, IEC & IEEE Codes: The Standards Behind Electrical Engineering
item.description: What IS, IEC and IEEE standards each actually govern, a working reference list across wiring, earthing, transformers, switchgear and solar PV, and the codes an EPC solar project reaches for most often.

item.title: Busbar Sizing: Why the Short-Circuit Check Often Governs, Not the Continuous Rating
item.description: Busbar cross-section from continuous current rating, then checked against short-circuit thermal withstand and electrodynamic force between conductors — plus enclosure heat dissipation.

item.title: Transformer and Generator Sizing: Why Motor Starting Decides the Genset, Not the Running Load
item.description: Transformer kVA from connected load and demand factor, and why standby generator sizing is governed by motor-starting voltage dip rather than the running load alone.

item.title: UPS Battery Sizing: Why the Nameplate Ah Never Matches What You Actually Get
item.description: Required battery Ah for a UPS from load and backup time, and why depth of discharge, aging, temperature and efficiency all derate the usable capacity well below nameplate.

item.title: Lighting Design by the Lumen Method: Why Luminaire Count Isn't Just Lumens ÷ Lux
item.description: Luminaire count for a target lux level using the lumen method, and why utilization factor and maintenance factor both derate raw lumen output before you get a real number.

item.title: LV Panel Estimating: Why a Budgetary BOQ Starts With the Incomer, Not the Steel
item.description: How an LV panel's busbar size, enclosure dimensions and budgetary BOQ cost all cascade from just two inputs: the incomer rating and the number of outgoing ways.

item.title: Current THD and K-Factor: Why Harmonic Distortion Derates Your Transformer
item.description: How current THD and K-factor are calculated from a harmonic spectrum, why K-factor weights higher harmonics more heavily, and why IEEE 519 limits aren't a single flat number.

item.title: Conduit Fill: Why 40% Isn't an Arbitrary Number
item.description: What the conduit fill percentage check is actually protecting against — pulling tension and jamming risk during installation, and heat dissipation once cables are in service.

item.title: Control Valve Cv Sizing: Why Oversizing Is the Most Common Mistake
item.description: Basic incompressible-flow control valve Cv sizing, and why an oversized valve hurts controllability even when it comfortably passes the required flow.

item.title: VFD Speed Scaling: Why Affinity Laws Make Small Speed Cuts Deliver Outsized Savings
item.description: Motor speed scaling with VFD output frequency, and why the pump/fan affinity laws mean modest speed reductions cut power consumption by a much larger percentage.

item.title: Duct Sizing: Why Velocity Limits Matter as Much as Airflow
item.description: Sizing ductwork for airflow, velocity and circular-equivalent diameter, and why designing for velocity limits matters as much as hitting the required airflow figure.

item.title: Chiller Capacity and COP: Where the Compressor's Work Actually Goes
item.description: Refrigeration cycle capacity, COP and compressor power, and why condenser heat rejection has to account for the compressor's work input, not just the cooling load alone.

item.title: NPSH Margin: Why 'NPSHa > NPSHr' Isn't Enough on Its Own
item.description: Pump hydraulic and shaft power sizing, and why an NPSH margin needs a safety factor beyond simply having available head exceed required head.

item.title: Belt Drive Sizing: Why the Speed Ratio Alone Doesn't Tell You the Tension
item.description: Belt drive speed ratio, belt velocity and shaft torque from pulley diameters and power, and why tension depends on wrap angle and friction, not just geometry.

item.title: Bolt Torque vs Preload: Why K-Factor Is the Number That Actually Matters
item.description: Bolt tightening torque from target preload using the short-form torque-tension relationship, and why the nut factor dominates the result far more than bolt grade.

item.title: Pipe Head Loss: Why Reynolds Number Decides Which Formula Applies
item.description: Pipe flow velocity, Reynolds number, friction factor and head loss, and why laminar and turbulent flow need genuinely different formulas rather than one general approximation.

item.title: Pipe Thermal Expansion: Why a 100m Run Moves More Than You'd Guess
item.description: Linear thermal expansion of a pipe run from material, length and temperature change, and why long runs in high-delta-T service need expansion loops, joints, or guided anchoring.

item.title: Prospective Short-Circuit Current: Why It Falls the Further You Are From Source
item.description: How prospective short-circuit current is calculated per IEC 60909, why it's highest at the transformer and drops downstream, and what that means for breaker interrupting ratings.

item.title: Voltage Drop in LV Feeders: Why It's a Chain, Not a Single Number
item.description: Why voltage drop accumulates through every segment of a feeder chain, the formula behind it, and why a cable sized fine for ampacity can still fail on voltage drop.

item.title: Breaker Selectivity: Why Two Correctly Rated Breakers Can Still Trip Together
item.description: What selectivity (discrimination) between breakers actually means, the Ir < Isd < Ii hierarchy behind it, and why overlapping trip curves cause both breakers to open for one fault.

item.title: kW, kVA, and kVAR: What Actually Separates Them
item.description: Real power, apparent power, and reactive power explained through the power triangle — why a transformer is rated in kVA and not kW, and a worked 3-phase example tying kW, kVA, and kVAR together.

item.title: Heat Pump Sizing Basics: Why Electrification Made This a Core Skill
item.description: Why heat pump sizing isn't the same exercise as furnace or AC sizing, what COP and capacity-at-temperature actually mean, and the balance-point logic that decides backup heat.

item.title: PID Controller Tuning Basics: What P, I, and D Actually Do
item.description: What the Proportional, Integral, and Derivative terms each actually correct for, why overshoot and oscillation happen, and a practical manual tuning sequence you can use in the field.

item.title: Deadband & Hysteresis: Why a Single Setpoint Isn't Enough
item.description: Why a switch needs two trip points instead of one — how deadband and hysteresis stop a control loop from chattering right at the setpoint.

item.title: Alarm Setpoint Bands: Why High and High-High Are Different Alarms
item.description: Why alarms come in High/High-High and Low/Low-Low pairs, not single trip points, and how a reset deadband on each keeps the alarm list from flooding operators.

item.title: Earthing & Grounding Systems Explained: Why Resistance Is the Whole Game
item.description: What an earthing system is actually protecting against, why grid resistance is the number that matters, the factors that drive it, and a practical checklist for getting it right on site.

item.title: Load Estimation: The First Step in Electrical Design
item.description: Why load estimation comes before anything else in an electrical project, how to calculate it by floor area, NEC VA/m² guide tables, and a full worked transformer-sizing example.

item.title: Cable Size & Current Capacity: A Practical Selection Guide
item.description: Approximate current-carrying capacity for copper and aluminium cables by cross-section, common house-wiring cable sizes by load, and the core-colour convention — with the factors that push the real number away from the table value.

item.title: Cable Glands: What They Do and How to Get the Selection Right
item.description: What a cable gland is actually holding together, the main gland types and their parts, a selection and quality-inspection checklist, an installation walkthrough, and an IP rating quick reference.

item.title: ANSI Relay Numbers: Common Protection Relay Functions
item.description: A working reference for the ANSI device numbers you'll actually run into on protection schemes — 50/51, 27/59, 87, 21, 67, 25 and more — what each one does and where it's typically applied.

item.title: How to Select a Digital Protection Relay
item.description: An 8-step working method for selecting a digital protection relay — identify the protected equipment, gather system data, match CT/VT inputs, select functions, size I/O, pick comms, verify environment, and coordinate — with a worked 11 kV feeder example.

item.title: Chilled Water HVAC Systems: How the Loop Actually Works
item.description: How a chilled water HVAC system moves heat from occupied zones all the way out to atmosphere — chiller, AHU cooling coil, pumps, and cooling tower, in one continuous loop.

item.title: Bearing Failures: Root Causes & Prevention
item.description: The five most common ways rolling-element bearings actually fail — spalling, lubrication breakdown, contamination, electrical erosion, and false brinelling — with the root cause and prevention for each.

item.title: Cavitation in Pumps: Causes, Warning Signs, and Prevention
item.description: What pump cavitation actually is, why NPSH available has to beat NPSH required, the field symptoms that give it away, and a practical prevention checklist.

item.title: Pump & Fan Affinity Laws: Why Speed Changes Cube the Power
item.description: Flow scales linearly with speed, head scales with the square, and power scales with the cube — the three affinity laws behind every VFD energy-savings claim, explained with the math and where they break down.

item.title: Reading a Centrifugal Pump Curve: Head, Flow, Efficiency & the BEP
item.description: How to read a manufacturer's pump curve — the head-capacity curve, efficiency islands, NPSHr curve, and why the system curve's intersection point decides where a pump actually operates.

item.title: Sensible vs. Latent Heat: Why Cooling Load Isn't Just Temperature
item.description: Why a cooling load calculation has two separate halves, what sensible and latent heat each actually cool, typical splits by space type, and why ignoring latent load leaves a room cold but clammy.

item.title: Soil Bearing Capacity: Why It Decides Your Footing Size, Not Just Column Load
item.description: Why footing area is set by the weaker of two numbers — column load and what the soil beneath it can safely carry — plus typical allowable bearing capacities and the factors that move them.

item.title: 4-20mA Current Loops: Why Industry Still Trusts an Analog Signal
item.description: Why 4-20mA beat 0-20mA and voltage signals for instrumentation, what live-zero actually protects against, how to convert a reading back to engineering units, and where the standard still wins over digital buses.

item.title: PV String Sizing: Why Voltage, Not Wattage, Decides Panels Per String
item.description: Why a cold morning can push string voltage past an inverter's limit, how the temperature coefficient drives that swing, and how to work out the maximum and minimum panels per string.

item.title: Earned Value Management: Reading Project Health From Three Numbers
item.description: Why 'on budget' and 'on schedule' need separate proof, what Planned Value, Earned Value and Actual Cost each measure, and how CPI and SPI turn them into an early warning system.

item.title: RACI Matrix Explained: Who's Responsible vs. Who's Accountable
item.description: Why projects stall when nobody owns a decision, what Responsible, Accountable, Consulted and Informed actually mean, and the one rule that keeps a RACI matrix from becoming useless.

item.title: Risk Register Basics: Turning Probability × Impact Into Priority
item.description: Why a risk list without scoring is just a list, how Probability × Impact turns gut feeling into a comparable number, and how to keep a register from becoming a document nobody reopens.

item.title: Permit to Work & LOTO: Why the Lock Belongs to the Person, Not the Job
item.description: What a permit to work actually authorizes, why lockout/tagout requires one lock per person rather than one lock per job, and how isolation points get verified before work starts.
